title: Best Job Application Trackers in 2026: Simplify vs Teal vs Huntr vs Notion vs a Spreadsheet
summary: We compared five ways to track job applications in 2026: Simplify, Teal, Huntr, Notion and a spreadsheet. Free plan limits, how jobs get added, prices, and who each one suits.
body_markdown:
It depends on how you apply. I'm a technical recruiter at Simplify, so I'll say the obvious part first: we make one of these trackers. If most of your applications go through company career sites, Simplify adds them to a free tracker as you submit them and can update their status from your Gmail. If you save jobs from job boards and want contacts and follow-up templates next to each one, Teal is the most complete free option. Huntr suits people who like a drag-and-drop board and are tracking fewer than 100 jobs. Notion or a spreadsheet suits people who want full control and don't mind typing everything in.


Every price and feature below comes from each company's own website or help center, checked on November 12, 2026. We didn't run a hands-on test of each tool, and where a page didn't say something, I say so.


## Why I care which tracker you use


Here's a question I ask in almost every early call: "Where else are you interviewing?" Candidates who track their search answer in a few seconds. Candidates who don't start scrolling through their inbox, and sometimes find out mid-call that they never heard back from half the places they applied.


A tracker won't get you interviews by itself. What it does is show you where your search is stalling, so you fix the right thing. That's the bar I used for everything below.


## The short version


- [Simplify](https://simplify.jobs/job-application-tracker?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=best-job-application-trackers-2026&utm_content=inline-1) if you want applications added to your tracker as you submit them, status suggestions from your inbox, and a chart of where your applications stop. The tracker is free.
- **Teal** if you mostly save jobs from job boards and want contacts, checklists and follow-up email templates next to each job. Tracking is unlimited on the free plan.
- **Huntr** if you want a Kanban board with contacts and a map of where you're applying. The free plan tracks up to 100 jobs.
- **Notion** if you want to design your own system and don't mind entering every application by hand.
- **A spreadsheet** if you're applying to a handful of roles and want something you fully control.

## Simplify


Simplify's[Job Tracker](https://simplify.jobs/job-application-tracker?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=best-job-application-trackers-2026&utm_content=inline-3) is free. The difference from the others is how applications get into it and how they stay current.


**Applications go in as you apply.** When you apply with the free[Copilot browser extension](https://simplify.jobs/copilot?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=best-job-application-trackers-2026&utm_content=inline-4) , Copilot adds the application to your tracker when it detects a supported submission. If it doesn't detect one, you can add the application yourself, save it from your matches or the job board, or import a CSV of whatever you were tracking before. If you connect Gmail, Simplify also flags applications it finds in your email that aren't in your tracker yet, so you can add the ones you forgot.


Copilot shows a submission confirmation and a link to Application History.


Keep applications organized by stage in Board view.


[Statuses update from your inbox.](https://help.simplify.jobs/articles/2140179-use-the-job-tracker?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=best-job-application-trackers-2026&utm_content=inline-5) Once Gmail is connected, Simplify matches recruiting emails to your applications and suggests status changes, such as moving a job to interviewing or rejected. You accept or dismiss each suggestion, or all of them at once. This is the part I'd care about most as a candidate. The recruiting email that says "we'd like to move forward" is easy to read on your phone and forget to log.


Review status changes found in your connected email, then accept or dismiss each suggestion.


Review detected submissions that are missing from your tracker.


**What you get for free**


- A Board view where you drag cards between stages, a List view for scanning rows, and a Chart view. You choose which optional columns to show, such as screen, withdrawn, ghosted and accepted.
- Search, filters for application date, job type, status and favorites, and sorting.
- A timeline for each application, with a date for each stage you reach.
- Notes, documents, salary details, saved application questions and a resume keyword match for each job.
- Bulk status changes, archiving and CSV export.
- [Flow Chart](https://simplify.jobs/job-application-tracker?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=best-job-application-trackers-2026&utm_content=inline-6) , a picture of how your applications move from applied to screening, interviewing, offer and accepted, and where they end up ghosted, rejected or withdrawn. It shows your average response time, ghost rate, application pace and conversion rate between stages. You can save a chart, share a link or export it as an image.


Keep stage dates, notes and job details together in each application.


The Flow Chart is the feature I'd point you to first. A list of 60 applications doesn't tell you much. A chart that shows most of them stopping before screening tells you to work on your resume and targeting. One that shows them stopping after interviews points to interview prep instead. Those are very different problems, and I see plenty of candidates rewriting a resume that was never the issue. Keep your statuses current, since the chart only knows what you've logged, and with a small number of applications, read the counts alongside the percentages.


A Flow Chart exported from Simplify's Job Tracker, shown with example data. In this search, more than half of the 60 applications got no response, so the place to start is getting more applications to screening.


See where your own applications stop. The tracker and Flow Chart are free.


[Get the free Job Tracker](https://simplify.jobs/job-application-tracker?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=best-job-application-trackers-2026&utm_content=button-1)


The iPhone app has the tracker and the Gmail status suggestions too. The Flow Chart and CSV import are on the web.


**What's paid**


[Simplify+](https://help.simplify.jobs/articles/5623502-whats-included-in-simplify-features-and-pricing?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=best-job-application-trackers-2026&utm_content=inline-7) adds AI resume tailoring, cover letters, AI answers to application questions, AI email drafts, networking and[Autopilot](https://simplify.jobs/ai-auto-apply?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=best-job-application-trackers-2026&utm_content=inline-8) . Autopilot fills out and submits applications for jobs you choose, on supported application systems such as Greenhouse, Ashby and Workable, with 20 credits a week. It doesn't cover every site, Workday included, and it submits without a separate review step, so it suits people who've already decided where to apply but don't have time to fill every form.


**Good to know:** Simplify's tracker doesn't have a contacts list or reminders. If keeping recruiter and referral contacts next to each job matters most to you, look at Teal or Huntr.


## Teal


Teal's Job Tracker lets you bookmark and track unlimited jobs for free. Its Chrome extension saves jobs from 40+ job boards, including Indeed, Glassdoor and BuiltIn, and picks up the pay listed in the job description.


Teal’s Job Tracker with five fictional applications. The list puts stages, dates and follow-ups in one view. Captured November 12, 2026.


Teal is strongest on organizing the work around each job: an excitement rating for prioritizing, notes on every job, contact and company, checklists for each stage, and email templates for following up. Its free plan includes one email template per job stage and the top 5 keywords from each job description. Teal+ unlocks unlimited keywords, unlimited templates and more resume analysis for $13 every 7 days, $29 every 30 days or $79 every 90 days, according to its pricing page.


Inside a Teal job: the Dates and Notes panels, with tabs for contacts, email templates and a checklist. Fictional sample data. Captured November 12, 2026.


If you're the kind of candidate who sends a thank-you note within a day and knows every recruiter's name, Teal is built for you.


**Good to know:** Teal's tracker page is about saving jobs from job boards. It doesn't mention autofilling applications or reading your inbox, so you'd update each job's status yourself.


## Huntr


Huntr's Job Tracker is built around a Kanban board. You save postings with the Chrome Job Clipper and drag them through stages. It also tracks contacts, interview dates, documents and multiple resumes, and has a map view that shows where your potential employers are.


Huntr’s board with five fictional applications across its default stages. Interview and Offer are sample statuses, not product-generated outcomes. Captured November 12, 2026.


Huntr's free plan tracks up to 100 jobs and includes unlimited application autofills, according to its pricing page. Huntr Pro removes the 100-job limit and adds more job search metrics for $40 a month, $90 every 3 months or $160 every 6 months. Huntr says there's no free trial.


Huntr’s job details bring application fields and activity logging together. The job and activity dates shown are fictional examples. Captured November 12, 2026.


**Good to know:** 100 jobs sounds like plenty until internship season, when many students send far more applications than that. Check whether the free limit covers your search before you start.


## Notion


Notion doesn't make a dedicated job tracker. You start from one of the community-made templates in its[Job Application Tracking gallery](https://www.notion.com/templates/category/job-application-tracking?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) , which lists more than 1,000, and customize it.


Notion’s Job Application Tracker (w/ Notion AI) template in table view, with four fictional entries. This is one template; other Notion trackers vary. Captured November 12, 2026. Template:[Notion](https://www.notion.com/templates/job-applications?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) .


That flexibility is the appeal. You choose the columns, statuses and views. The tradeoff is that every application goes in by hand, and nothing updates when you apply or hear back. Notion's free plan covers personal use, and Plus costs $10 per member a month. Notion says the Plus plan with a one-member limit is free for students and educators.


The same Notion database in its built-in board view, grouped by stage. Fictional sample data. Captured November 12, 2026.


## A spreadsheet


A Google Sheet or Excel file is free, private and works offline. For a search of 10 or 20 roles, it's often all you need.


Gemini in Google Sheets helped create the example below, including its layout, status dropdowns and summary counts. You still have to organize your applications and update their statuses manually, which becomes more work as you apply widely. These columns are a useful starting point:


- Company and role
- Link to the posting
- Date applied
- Status (applied, screening, interview, offer, rejected, no response)
- Contact or referral
- Next step and date


A Google Sheets tracker with five fictional applications, status dropdowns and next steps. Layout and formatting were generated with Gemini in Sheets. Captured November 12, 2026.


## Which one should you use?


Start with how you apply. If most of your applications go through company career sites, a tracker that fills itself in as you apply and checks your inbox saves the most time, which is what Simplify is built for. If you mostly save postings from job boards and want help with follow-ups and contacts, Teal is the most complete free option. If you like a visual board and are applying to fewer than 100 jobs, Huntr's free plan works well. If you want full control, Notion or a spreadsheet will do, as long as you keep it updated.


Whatever you pick, update statuses when you hear back. A tracker is only as useful as its last update, and the candidates who keep theirs current are the ones who can tell me exactly where they stand.


## Common questions


**What is the best free job application tracker?** It depends on how you apply. Simplify's tracker is free, adds applications as you submit them with its Copilot extension, and suggests status changes from your Gmail. Teal's free plan tracks unlimited jobs saved from job boards. Huntr's free plan tracks up to 100 jobs on a Kanban board.


**Can a job tracker update itself from my email?** Simplify's can. Once you connect Gmail, it matches recruiting emails to your tracked applications and suggests status changes for you to accept or dismiss. It also flags applications it finds in your email that aren't in your tracker yet.


**How much do Teal and Huntr cost?** Both trackers have free plans. Teal+ costs $13 every 7 days, $29 every 30 days or $79 every 90 days. Huntr Pro costs $40 a month, $90 every 3 months or $160 every 6 months, and removes the free plan's 100-job limit.


**Can you use Notion as a job tracker?** Yes. Notion's template gallery has more than 1,000 community-made job application tracking templates. You enter and update each application by hand.


**Should I use a spreadsheet to track job applications?** A spreadsheet works for a small search. Once you're applying to dozens of roles, a tracker that adds applications for you and shows where they stop saves time and keeps statuses current.
